edges.description: Patient IgG and anti-alpha3 antibodies can reduce functional ganglionic AChR current and surface receptor availability.
Sensory and central manifestations co-occur in seropositive cohorts, but whether the same antibodies, another immune target, or a comorbid process causes them is unresolved.
Reduced ganglionic cholinergic signaling disrupts sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric autonomic outflow.
Loss of sympathetic vasoconstrictor responses causes neurogenic orthostatic hypotension.
Enteric and parasympathetic failure disrupt gastrointestinal propulsion and coordination.
Gastrointestinal autonomic failure can markedly delay gastric emptying.
Parasympathetic and coordinated bladder autonomic failure can impair emptying.
Postganglionic sympathetic cholinergic failure reduces sweat-gland activation.
Parasympathetic secretomotor failure reduces saliva production.
Parasympathetic secretomotor failure reduces tear production.
Abnormal sympathetic vasomotor control can produce dependent acrocyanosis.
Parasympathetic pupillary efferent failure impairs light-induced constriction.
Autonomic failure can impair erection in affected males.
The causal route from AAG-associated autoimmunity to sensory symptoms remains unresolved.
